about: Research prose behind each built-in device model's animation figures: what the API does, its risks, and the sources. scripts/ci/led-fixtures.mjs merges these into scripts/ci/tests/fixtures/device-models.json as `animation.notes` / `animation.sources`; the runtime built-ins in src/lib/devices.ts deliberately carry neither, so the bundle holds only what rendering needs. `unverified` in a note marks a memory.

vestaboard_flagship.notes: Frames are written by FiestaBoard one at a time (transition plugins step frame-by-frame); the board's own flap cascade animates each write. ~1 frame/s is the practical ceiling for legible flap motion on the local API. Cloud connections are additionally floored by FiestaBoard at one write per 15 s (transport policy, not device capability).
sources: FiestaBoard core transition runner and send floor (fiestaboard#2190)

divoom_pixoo64.notes: Verified on a Pixoo 64 (hardware 92), camera-timed, in two labs (2026-10-04 and 2026-10-05). FiestaBoard STREAMS on this device: every frame is its own single-frame Draw/SendHttpGif push (PicNum 1), which plays once with no overlay and no loop, and the last frame always lands cleanly. maxFps 5 is the measured stream rate: each push takes ~0.19 s whatever the frame size (64 px and 32 px alike); paced at 5 fps, 19 of 20 frames displayed (12 of 12 at 4 fps); back-to-back pushes reach ~4.2-5 fps with an occasional dropped middle frame; 6 fps cannot be sent. Two requests in flight drop frames, and Draw/CommandList shows only its last frame and is no faster, so frames go one at a time in order. Core-planned flip, slide, wipe, cascade, dissolve and fade, streamed at 5 fps, all displayed as intended (lab 2). Channel/SetBrightness answers in ~75 ms, so a fade through black (dim, swap, brighten) takes ~1.1 s. Why not an uploaded animation (lab 1): Draw/SendHttpGif uploads (one POST per frame, PicNum frames, PicOffset index, PicSpeed ms per frame, PicData base64 RGB888 row-major from the top left, PicWidth 64) LOOP FOREVER with no play-once flag; any upload longer than ~1.2 s (more than ~3 frames) shows a LOADING overlay; landing on a still after an animation keeps the old loop running with frame 0 replaced for ~5 s. PicID: a push displays only if PicID > the last accepted one (skipping ahead is fine); a reused or lower PicID still answers error_code 0 but is silently ignored. Draw/GetHttpGifId returns the next id (0 right after a reset). Draw/ResetHttpGifId does not clear the screen and needs no wait afterwards. Not verified: the community report of a freeze after ~300 pushes without a reset (the plugin resets every 32), and behaviour on other firmware. mDNS: the device advertises nothing.
sources: FiestaBoard hardware lab on a Pixoo 64, 2026-10-04 (camera-timed; fiestaboard-output--divoom-pixoo PR #1)
FiestaBoard hardware lab 2 on a Pixoo 64, 2026-10-05 (camera-timed single-frame streaming, brightness ramps, core-planned transitions)
https://doc.divoom-gz.com/web/#/12?page_id=93 (Draw/SendHttpGif; read via the ShowDoc JSON API)

ulanzi_tc001_awtrix.notes: Custom apps take `draw` ops (dp/dl/dr/df/dc/dfc/dt/db) over HTTP or MQTT; `db` with a full 8×32 bitmap returned ErrorParsingJson (#214). TSPEED (app transition) defaults to 500 ms, ATIME 7 s. No stated rate limit; the push rate is UNMEASURED (no test device), so the model is held at a nominal 2 fps — below every animated entry's minimum — and stays on snap, letting the firmware's own Slide transition carry the change.

wled_32x32.notes: DDP on UDP 4048 (480 RGB pixels per 1440-byte datagram; 1024 LEDs = 3 datagrams a frame) holds 25–40 fps on an ESP32; E1.31 is documented at '25 ms (40 fps)' for ≤ 510 LEDs; WLED_FPS default 42. The JSON `seg.i` route is HTTP + parse per call and not for this.

hub75_64x32.notes: rpi-rgb-led-matrix refreshes 'typically in the hundreds of Hertz' (three 128×64 panels: 410 Hz); a Pi daemon fed over the network (flaschen-taschen style) holds 30–60 fps.

hub75_128x64.notes: As hub75_64x32; a 128×64 chain still refreshes above 100 Hz on a Pi 4.

max7219_4in1.notes: A 32×8 frame is 32 bytes over SPI; MD_Parola's setSpeed() runs animations at any ms interval ('zero to run as fast as possible'). Hundreds of fps locally (unverified figure); the bridge from a host to the module is custom, so the figure assumes you own it.

p10_hub12_32x16.notes: HUB12 modules are scanned by the host microcontroller (DMD32 / DMD_STM32, 30–70 µs row on-time); a frame over serial is 64 bytes. No standard host protocol, so the figure assumes you own the bridge.

tidbyt_tronbyt.notes: Tronbyt server: POST /v0/devices/{id}/push with a base64 WebP, displayTimeSec default 30; devices poll /next and loop the animation. Pixlet render.Root(delay=ms) sets the frame time (50 ms default — unverified). Tidbyt's cloud is rate-limited with no published number. One WebP per message change, so a flip is a sequence at 80 ms per step with no half-flaps.
